facts.fact: Kiran, 25, stayed on at Garh Neshar after Book 1 and works as Ila's chain-man through the summer survey into winter; his sister Meera is betrothed to Ila's brother Rohan, so he will be Ila's relation by marriage.
facts.why: needed because the outline names Kiran as Ila's summer chain-man and Book 1 left him at Garh Neshar with Ila to mend.

facts.fact: The tower's north landing has a half-height step set into the boards that people step over without counting. Kunal's family counts the stair as thirty-nine steps ('children's count, for ghosts'); Ila counts forty. The north wall there is colder and sweats slightly.
facts.why: needed to plant the clue at the peak (technique 11) and the stair-count correction the outline requires.

facts.fact: Garh Neshar's builder, in family songs, is a drunk mason named Dev.
facts.why: needed so Kunal can give the outline's 'drunk mason built it crooked' answer with a concrete detail.

facts.fact: Ila's pace is two and a half spans, calibrated against the brass rule at Taravan at nineteen and a chalk line her father laid each spring. The tower's north face is twenty-two paces outside, and the inside room is a full pace short after wall thickness is allowed for; she allows half a span for sloppy plaster and records two spans.
facts.why: needed to reconcile 'a full pace shorter' with the field-book note 'two spans out of true'.

facts.fact: The hill-council guards wear undyed wool with a blue cord on the shoulder; the Winter Crossing Law notice on the gate shows the Shilak post's brown seal and the hill council's blue seal, and a goat has been scratched in the margin by the third line.
facts.why: needed for the society-at-a-walk beat showing the licence law's two seals.
